### 2.4 Bio-Plastics

Bio-plastics are polymeric materials manufactured partially or entirely from renewable biological resources rather than conventional petroleum-based feedstocks. Typical sources include corn starch, sugarcane, cellulose, vegetable oils, and materials produced through biological processes involving microorganisms [17, 18]. Depending on their chemical composition and production route, bio-plastics may be classified as bio-based, biodegradable, or both.

Bio-plastics are produced through chemical or biological processes that convert natural raw materials into moldable polymers suitable for conventional plastic manufacturing techniques. Common examples include polylactic acid (PLA) and poly hydroxy alkanotes (PHA), which can be processed using extrusion, injection molding, and thermoforming methods similar to those employed for traditional plastics [19]. This compatibility with existing processing technologies has facilitated the industrial adoption of bio-plastics and supports their integration within sustainability and circular economy frameworks [20].

Bio-plastics are currently utilized in a wide range of applications, including packaging, medical products, consumer goods, and selected engineering components. Continuous research and development efforts aim to enhance their mechanical properties, thermal stability, and durability in order to broaden their applicability in more demanding environments [21].
